frequency_question: How often does a congressional resolution to block a major executive international agreement successfully pass both chambers and overcome or avoid a presidential veto within the statutory window?
membership_rule: Includes formal nuclear, arms sales, or major trade agreements submitted to the U.S. Congress under statutory review procedures where a joint resolution of disapproval is legally permitted. Excludes standard treaties requiring 2/3 Senate ratification.

skeleton: Submissions of major contentious executive-legislative foreign policy agreements subject to disapproval mechanics since the 1970s
multiplier: Estimated 10 major distinct contentious review cycles over 50 years, yielding very few successful veto overrides or veto-proof blocks.
validity_reason: Constitutional veto thresholds and statutory review mechanics remain stable across administrations.
